correctness.rationale: Inspectable diff shows core scaffolding (PR arg validation, allow-list load, INTERVAL/QUIET_WINDOW/MAX_WAIT defaults, gh pr view polling loop, RESULT=/HEAD= stdout, and exit codes 0/2/3/4) but multiple task-contract gaps remain. CONVERGED exits solely when open_bot_threads length is zero without checking whether participating allow-listed bots are terminal for the current head. QUIET_ELAPSED can fire on the first loop when no reviews exist because latest_event falls back to timestamp 0, making QUIET_ELAPSED equal to NOW and immediately >= QUIET_WINDOW even while open bot threads remain. latest_event is derived only from review createdAt, not the broader actionable-event set described in the prompt fallback. SHA_CHANGED compares each snapshot head only against the session INITIAL_SHA rather than checking head immediately before and after each snapshot fetch. Dead unused get_pr_snapshot() still hardcodes bot identities, contradicting the file-driven allow-list requirement.

quality.rationale: Required doc surfaces are updated appropriately: pr-resolve-all.md adds a preferred helper step plus preserved time-based fallback, and AI_REPO_GUIDE.md documents invocation. The helper script is readable shell with clear header contract comments. Quality is reduced by leftover draft code (unused get_pr_snapshot with hardcoded bots, inline WIP comments questioning convergence semantics), fragile allow-list-to-jq plumbing via pipe-delimited regex, and a thin existence-only check script (106-pr-poll-helper.sh) that does not assert behavioral contracts.

process.rationale: Diff is focused on six on-task files with no evident scope noise; all required paths and both doc companions are present per objective evidence; pre-#321 boundary and in-memory-only constraint are respected; the documented time-based fallback is retained in pr-resolve-all.md. Minor deduction for incomplete verification wiring (objective test_wiring 1/2 patterns) and no evidence of full test.sh or bats integration beyond minimal file presence.

reliability.rationale: Verification discipline is thin relative to the exit contract. Bats coverage exercises only missing-PR and missing-allowlist API_ERROR paths; there are no mock-gh tests for CONVERGED, SHA_CHANGED, QUIET_ELAPSED, or TIMEOUT despite those being the primary behavioral paths. Objective evidence shows bats_poll_helper and full_test_sh skipped, test_wiring only 1/2 patterns matched, and no runtime pass logs in the bundle—so contract-path correctness is structurally unproven beyond bash -n and lint on the helper itself.

citations.claim: hard_gate_pass is true, so subjective categories are scored normally rather than fail-closed to zero.
test_wiring passed 1/2 patterns; bats_poll_helper and full_test_sh were skipped in bundle-only grading.
Task requires CONVERGED when participating expected bots are terminal for the current head and no unresolved actionable bot-authored review threads remain.
CONVERGED branch exits 0 when OPEN_THREADS equals zero without inspecting participating-bot terminal state.
latest_event is computed only from reviews[].createdAt; when absent LATEST_EVENT_TS defaults to 0 so QUIET_ELAPSED can satisfy QUIET_WINDOW immediately while open threads may still exist.
Poll loop compares CURRENT_SHA to INITIAL_SHA each iteration rather than capturing head immediately before and after a single snapshot fetch.
Unused get_pr_snapshot() hardcodes allow-listed bot logins while get_pr_snapshot_v2 reads scripts/lib/bot-allowlist.txt.
pr-resolve-all.md section 2.1 documents preferred bash scripts/pr-resolve-all-poll.sh invocation and retains the documented time-based fallback.
scripts/tests/pr-resolve-all-poll.bats contains only two tests for missing PR number and missing allowlist API_ERROR paths.
scripts/checks/106-pr-poll-helper.sh verifies helper and allow-list file existence but not behavioral contract.
Six changed files limited to helper, allow-list, bats, check, and required doc surfaces.
